page.layout: One page of text. Running head at the top, with the page number above it. Below a horizontal rule: the title block, centred (APODICTICA RESPONSI, "Ad scopum.", APPLICATIO.). Then running text in one column, opening with a woodcut initial. Catchword at the lower right. No margin notes.

main_text.l: de, quod angelus Gabriel apud Danielem tempus visionis
obsignandæ[?] & adventus Christi incluserit intra septuaginta
hebdomadas: dixeratque post hebdomadas septem &
sexaginta duas (id est lxix) excindendum fuisse
Messiam ducem: Dan. 9: 24. 25. quæ res proin ita tem-pori
alligata fuit, ut sine subversione veritatis propheticæ
anticipari non potuerit, æque minus ac in
posteriora differri.
APODICTICA
RESPONSI
APPLICATIO.
ESt in hâc pericopâ responsum divinum, singulari
modo propagatum, dum in tabulis
exaratum fuit, & juxta præceptum Dei in locis
publicis affixum, quo omnes etiam curfum lo-
gant. Hoc responsum Dei relatum est ad dilceptatio-
nem Prophetæ, nomine justorum in populo factam:
in quo dubia solvuntur, & hæsitationes ex follicito-rum
animis satis solidè eximuntur.
1. Prima hæsitatio fuit, si Chaldæus ita immittatur
in Judæos, fore ut populus Dei segregatus à gentibus
pereat, emoriatur, & non amplius superfit in orbe:
atque ita actum erit cum visione legis & prophetarum:

page.notes: The word after "visionis" at the line end is printed "ol-" with a hyphen, and the next line begins "obsignandæ"; the first letter is ambiguous in the scan (b or l), so it is marked [?]. "lxix" in the parenthesis is printed with spacing that could also read as "lx ix"; transcribed as printed-looking "lxix". A small stray mark stands above "pereat" in the text; not transcribed. The woodcut initial "E" is joined to "St" as "ESt". The running head is taken from the small-caps line at the top, without the page number.
